title: Albright — IHH content reconciliation
header: Private editorial working note, 17 October 2026. **REQUIRES HUMAN SIGN-OFF.** This is not approved visitor copy. No changes to `inductees/albright/copy.md` are authorized by this note.

IHH starting page: [madeleine-albright](https://immigranthallofhonor.org/inductees/inductee-madeleine-albright/), retrieved during this review. Line references identify the retrieved text view, not a stable page anchor. Facts are inventoried below in IHH’s order. Compound rows retain all their components; NOT VERIFIED applies to each component unless a narrower status is explicitly stated.

Independent source read: [US Department of State, Office of the Historian](https://history.state.gov/departmenthistory/people/albright-madeleine-korbel). A page being available does not verify every claim on IHH.

OH: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, “Madeleine Korbel Albright”
GU: Georgetown University, Mortara Center, “The Honorable Madeleine K. Albright”

L9.claim: U.S. Name: Madeleine Jana Korbel Albright
evidence: Madeleine Korbel Albright, 64th Secretary of State
L9.note: The State Department uses “Madeleine Korbel Albright”. The middle name “Jana” is not in the retrieved sources.

evidence: Albright was born Marie Jean “Madlenka” Korbel on May 15, 1937, in Prague, Czechoslovakia.
L10.note: The State Department’s historian gives “Marie Jean ‘Madlenka’ Korbel”. IHH’s “Marie Jana” may be the Czech form of the same name. IHH should either use the State Department form or explain the variant.

evidence: Albright was born Marie Jean “Madlenka” Korbel on May 15, 1937, in Prague, Czechoslovakia.
L11.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from U.S. Department of State.

L12.note: The year is confirmed by the State Department. The exact date (March 23) and place (Washington, D.C.) were not in the retrieved text: two news sites tried were blocked or refused access.

L14.claim: Education: Wellesley College (B.A in Political Science 1959), Columbia University (Masters and Ph. D in Public Law and Government 1976)
evidence: earned a B.A. in political science with honors from Wellesley College in 1959
She earned the Ph.D. in Public Law and Government at Columbia University in 1976.
Master’s and Doctorate degrees from Columbia University
L14.note: The master’s degree is confirmed; its year is not given.

evidence: Madeleine K. Albright was a professor, author, diplomat and businesswoman
L15.note: Status revised 17 Oct 2026: “Author” is confirmed; “Politician” is not in the source, which says “professor, author, diplomat and businesswoman”. IHH could use “Diplomat, Author”.

L16.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from U.S. Department of State.

L25.claim: Member of President Carter’s National Security Council (1978 – 1981)
evidence: From 1978 to 1981, she served as a staff member in the White House under President Jimmy Carter and on the National Security Council
L25.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from U.S. Department of State.

L26.claim: President of the Center of National Policy (1989 – 1992)
evidence: From 1989 to 1992, she served as President of the Center for National Policy.
L26.note: Name note: it is the Center for National Policy (IHH writes “Center of National Policy”).

L27.claim: U.S Ambassador to the United Nations (1993 – 1997)
evidence: Representative of the U.S.A. to the United Nations Appointed: January 27, 1993
L27.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from U.S. Department of State.

L28.claim: First female U.S. Secretary of State under President Clinton (1997 – 2001)
evidence: was nominated to be the first woman Secretary of State by President William Jefferson Clinton
L28.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from U.S. Department of State.

L29.claim: Chair of the National Democratic Institute for International Affairs (2001)
evidence: She also chaired the National Democratic Institute
L29.note: Chair confirmed; the 2001 start year is not in this source.

L30.claim: Board of Trustees for the Aspen Institute (2002)
L30.note: Not found in the retrieved sources: none of the three (State Department historian, Wellesley, Georgetown) mentions the Aspen Institute board.

L31.claim: President of the Truman Scholarship Foundation (2003)
evidence: served as the president of the Truman Scholarship Foundation
L31.note: Role confirmed; the 2003 year is not in this source.

L32.claim: Chair for NATO New Strategic Concept development (2009)
L32.note: Not found in the retrieved sources. NATO’s own record of the 2009–10 Group of Experts was not retrieved.

L33.claim: Author of seven books, including public policy and memoir
evidence: She was the author of seven New York Times bestselling books including her autobiography, Madam Secretary: A Memoir (2003).
L33.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from Wellesley College.

L40.claim: Order of the White Lion (1997, Czech)
L40.note: No Czech presidential-office record of the Order of the White Lion was retrieved. Our own profile also lists this as an open item.

L41.claim: Induction into the National Women’s Hall of Fame (1998)
L41.note: No record from the National Women’s Hall of Fame was retrieved.

L42.note: No record from the Hanno R. Ellenbogen Citizenship Award was retrieved.

L43.note: No record from the Fulbright Association was retrieved.

evidence: Dr. Albright received the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor, from President Obama on May 29, 2012.

## Biography and captions

**NOT VERIFIED as a whole.** Additional narrative claims to check individually: First female Secretary of State; Clinton service 1997–2001; family flight from communism; graduate study; UN appointment; NATO enlargement, Kosovo and democracy work; later professor, writer and adviser. Any repeated facts inherit only the scoped evidence above. Interpretive praise is not a verifiable historical fact and should receive editorial review. Image captions and identification remain subject to the item-level rights and identity review in the manifest.

## Integration and open items

Carry forward the Facts, Achievements and Honours headings as above when IHH approves the supported entries. Do not copy unresolved entries into the public profile. The existing narrative is unchanged; a public structured block is pending approval of its factual content. Do not link this note from visitor pages.
